title: D8763

page_data.en:
Translation of French Police Report
dated September 30, 1938.

Statement of Anne G. DEMINA, aged 31, Russian residing
at 118/9 Route des **〔此处转录不清〕**, Apartment 2; dancing
partner at the Little Club, Bubbling Well Road.

At 7 a.m. yesterday I went to the "Dejourny"
Restaurant, 771/1 Avenue Joffre, where I remained all
day. A Russian named NOSKOFF alias "Mongol" came in
with a uniformed British soldier who sat at my table.
At 9 p.m. I returned to my apartment in the company of
the soldier who passed the night with me.

At 7 a.m. this morning the soldier left and I
immediately observed that a nickel-plated watch, value
$6, of Japanese manufacture, that was on my dressing
table, had disappeared. This watch belongs to an
American marine.

Towards noon to-day, I again made my way to the
"Dejourny" Restaurant, where I saw the same British
soldier, now in plain clothes. At first he denied
having stolen the watch but in the finish admitted the
theft claiming that he was under the influence of
drink when he did it. He also stated he had pawned the
watch.

It was explained to me in the restaurant that the
soldier was always in the company of NOSKOFF and that
in all probability the latter had furnished the soldier
with the civilian clothing and had assisted him in
pawning the watch.

The British soldier promised to go and redeem the
watch, but having left at 1 p.m. he did not return
which compelled me to complain to the Police.

Signed :- DEMINA.
page_data.zh:
法文警务报告译文
日期：1938年9月30日。

安娜·G·杰米娜（Anne G. DEMINA）陈述，31岁，俄罗斯人，居住于**〔此处转录不清〕**路118/9号2室；静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）“小俱乐部”（Little Club）舞女。

昨天上午7时，我前往霞飞路771/1号的“德茹尔尼”（Dejourny）餐馆，并在那里停留了一整天。一名绰号“蒙古人”（Mongol）、名为诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）的俄罗斯人与一名身穿制服的英国士兵一同进入，该士兵坐在我的桌旁。晚上9时，我与该士兵一同返回我的公寓，他与我共度一夜。

今天上午7时，该士兵离开，我随即发现放在我梳妆台上的一块镀镍手表不见了，该表价值6美元，日本制造。这块手表属于一名美国海军陆战队员。

今天中午左右，我再次前往“德茹尔尼”餐馆，在那里我看到了同一名英国士兵，此时他已换上便服。起初他否认偷窃了手表，但最后承认了盗窃行为，声称作案时处于醉酒状态。他还称已将手表典当。

餐馆里有人向我解释，这名士兵总是与诺斯科夫在一起，后者很可能为士兵提供了便服，并协助其典当了手表。

该英国士兵承诺去赎回手表，但他于下午1时离开后并未返回，这迫使我向警方报案。

签名：- 杰米娜（DEMINA）。

page_data.en:
September 30, 1938.

Statement of Eugene P. KOUZMINSKY, aged 25, Russian,
residing at Room 10, 697/2 Avenue Joffre, baggage
man of the "City Express Company" Apt. 3, 55 Rue
Moliere.
------------------

At 6.15 a.m. to-day I went to the "Dejourny"
Restaurant, 771/1 Avenue Joffre where the British
soldier with whom I was drinking yesterday, put in an
appearance about 7 a.m. Some minutes later NOSKOFF
alias "Mongol" also arrived. I drank vodka with NOSKOFF
while the soldier did not drink at all. Later about 8
a.m., we all left and went to a pawnshop at No.7 Route
Pere Robert when the soldier took a watch from his
pocket and in "Mongol's" company, pawned it for $4.
I observed NOSKOFF write something on the ticket. We
then left the pawn shop and made our way to the "Rouss"
Restaurant on Route Pere Robert where the soldier said
he did not wish to remain any longer in the Army but
desired to live among Russians. He took two medals
from his pocket and gave one to me and one to NOSKOFF
to whom he also handed a copper ring.

As the soldier was always asking for a suit of
civilian clothing, I asked for 30 cents and then went
to the Chinese laundryman on Route Vallon near "Jean"
Restaurant to whom I had given a shirt and a pair of
trousers to wash.

Having secured these garments I brought them to
TOMMY (the British soldier) and we proceeded to the
"Poland" Restaurant, 771/15 Avenue Joffre where we
stored the waterproof and uniform cap of the soldier,
who was now in civilian clothing. NOSKOFF proposed
to him that he secure some shoes and in company with a
Netherlander named PELEN (?) we went along to 682/6B
page_data.zh:
1938年9月30日。

叶夫根尼·P·库兹明斯基（Eugene P. KOUZMINSKY）陈述，25岁，俄罗斯人，居住于霞飞路697/2号10室；“城市快运公司”（City Express Company）行李员，该公司地址为莫利哀路（Rue Moliere）55号3室。
---

今天上午6时15分，我前往霞飞路771/1号的“德茹尔尼”餐馆，昨天与我一起喝酒的那名英国士兵大约在上午7时出现。几分钟后，绰号“蒙古人”的诺斯科夫也到达。我与诺斯科夫一起喝伏特加，而那名士兵滴酒未沾。后来大约在上午8时，我们一起离开，前往贝当路（Route Pere Robert）7号的一家当铺，当时士兵从口袋里掏出一块手表，在“蒙古人”的陪同下，以4美元的价格将其典当。我观察到诺斯科夫在当票上写了些什么。随后我们离开当铺，前往贝当路上的“鲁斯”（Rouss）餐馆，在那里士兵表示他不想再留在军队里，而是希望生活在俄罗斯人中间。他从口袋里拿出两枚勋章，一枚给我，一枚给诺斯科夫，他还递给诺斯科夫一个铜戒指。

由于这名士兵一直索要一套便服，我要了30美分，然后前往瓦隆路（Route Vallon）“让”（Jean）餐馆附近的中国洗衣工处，我之前曾将一件衬衫和一条裤子交给他清洗。

拿到这些衣物后，我把它们带给汤米（TOMMY，即那名英国士兵），我们随后前往霞飞路771/15号的“波兰”（Poland）餐馆，我们将士兵的雨衣和军帽存放在那里，此时他已换上便服。诺斯科夫建议他去弄双鞋，于是我们与一名名叫佩伦（PELEN，音译）的荷兰人一起前往勃艮第路（Rue Bourgeat）682/6B号

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Rue Bourgeat where Noskoff took someone's black shoes
and gave them to the Englishman, after which they went
by ricsha to the "Dejourny" Restaurant, 771/1 Avenue
Joffre, I following on foot. There the three of us
drank beer together. Later we all went to a beer-hall
called "Marco" at the corner of Avenue Joffre and
Route Pere Robert.

About noon we separated on Avenue Joffre near
Route Pere Robert and just before he left NOSKOFF went
to the "Poland" Restaurant from where he took the sol-
dier's shoes and waterproof and tried to sell them.
Not being successful in disposing of them in the French
Concession, he met me at 12.45 p.m., gave me these
objects and told me to sell them for $4.

I then went to the Settlement and sold the shoes
to a hawker in Peking Road for sixty cents.

I was unable to sell the waterproof because it
was a military model and bore a number.

I returned to Lane 771, Avenue Joffre where I
again met Noskoff to whom I gave fifty cents retaining
ten cents for myself.

Later I took the military cap from PIERRE
IVANOVITCH owner of the "Dejourny" Restaurant and just
as I was carrying this cap and the waterproof, I was
arrested by a French Police detective accompanied by
members of the British Military Police.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

勃艮第路，在那里诺斯科夫拿了某人的黑鞋并给了那个英国人，之后他们乘人力车前往霞飞路771/1号的“德茹尔尼”餐馆，我则步行跟随。在那里，我们三人一起喝了啤酒。后来我们都去了位于霞飞路与贝当路拐角处的一家名为“马可”（Marco）的啤酒馆。

大约中午时分，我们在霞飞路靠近贝当路的地方分开，就在诺斯科夫离开前，他去了“波兰”餐馆，从那里取走了士兵的鞋子和雨衣，并试图出售。由于在法租界未能成功脱手，他在下午12时45分遇到我，将这些物品交给我，让我以4美元的价格卖掉。

随后我前往公共租界，在北京路以60美分的价格将鞋子卖给了一名小贩。

我未能卖出雨衣，因为那是军用款式，上面印有编号。

我回到霞飞路771弄，再次遇到诺斯科夫，我给了他50美分，自己留下了10美分。

后来，我从“德茹尔尼”餐馆老板皮埃尔·伊万诺维奇（PIERRE IVANOVITCH）那里拿走了军帽，正当我拿着这顶帽子和雨衣时，我被一名法国警探逮捕，当时有英国宪兵队成员陪同。

page_data.en:
September 30, 1938.

I, the undersigned, Vladimir NOSKOFF, aged 26,
residing at 164 Route Vallon, do hereby state that at
6 p.m. September 29, 1938 I met in a restaurant at No. 1,
Lane 771 Avenue Joffre, a British soldier whom I had
known previously as "Tommy." We drank six bottles of
beer and one and a half bottles of vodka together. A cer-
tain Eugene KOUZMINSKY was in our company. At 7 p.m.
I made my way to a brothel behind Joffre Police Station
and stayed there for the night. Getting up at 7.30 a.m.
I left the brothel and proceeded to the above mentioned
restaurant where at 8 a.m. I found the English soldier
and KOUZMINSKY. Both were slightly under the influence
of drink. TOMMY was in uniform: - Khaki shirt, khaki
pants, khaki puttees, dark brown boots, military water-
proof and cap. I proposed to the Englishman to buy a
bottle of beer, each of us paying thirty cents. When
we were drinking TOMMY said that he no longer wished to
remain in the British Army, that his mother would be
sending him £48 per month and that he would remain with
the Russians in Shanghai. Seeing that he had no more
money, TOMMY declared that it would be necessary for
him to pawn the watch which he had on his left wrist;
this watch was round and of white metal. I advised him
not to pawn his belongings, telling him that my mother
would give me some money but he declined to listen and
insisted on going to a pawnshop. The three of us,
TOMMY, KOUZMINSKY and myself, then proceeded to a pawn
shop at No.7 Route Pere Robert. About 11 a.m. TOMMY and
myself entered the pawnshop while KOUZMINSKY remained
outside. TOMMY took off his wrist watch and pawned it
for $4. At TOMMY's request, I wrote in Russian on the
ticket the date of pawning and the type of object.
page_data.zh:
1938年9月30日。

本人，弗拉基米尔·诺斯科夫（Vladimir NOSKOFF），26岁，居住于瓦隆路164号，特此声明：1938年9月29日下午6时，我在霞飞路771弄1号的一家餐馆遇到了一名英国士兵，我之前认识他，叫他“汤米”。我们一起喝了六瓶啤酒和一瓶半伏特加。叶夫根尼·库兹明斯基（Eugene KOUZMINSKY）当时与我们在一起。晚上7时，我前往霞飞路巡捕房后面的一家妓院，并在那里过夜。早上7时30分起床后，我离开妓院，前往上述餐馆，在上午8时找到了那名英国士兵和库兹明斯基。两人都略带醉意。汤米身穿制服：卡其色衬衫、卡其色长裤、卡其色绑腿、深棕色靴子、军用雨衣和军帽。我向这名英国人提议买一瓶啤酒，每人付30美分。喝酒时，汤米说他不再想留在英国军队里，说他母亲每月会寄给他48英镑，他将留在上海的俄罗斯人中间。看到他没钱了，汤米宣称必须把他左手腕上的手表典当掉；这块表是圆形的，白色金属材质。我建议他不要典当自己的财物，告诉他我母亲会给我一些钱，但他不听劝告，坚持要去当铺。于是我们三人，汤米、库兹明斯基和我，前往贝当路7号的一家当铺。上午11时左右，汤米和我进入当铺，而库兹明斯基留在外面。汤米摘下腕表，以4美元的价格典当。应汤米的要求，我用俄语在当票上写下了典当日期和物品类型。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

After that the three of us proceeded to the "Rouss"
Restaurant on Route Pere Robert.
    In this restaurant we ordered a bottle of beer
and a half-bottle of vodka. In the restaurant a little
later TOMMY asked that a civilian suit be found for him.
KOUZMINSKY told him that if he gave him thirty cents,
he could bring him a shirt and a pair of pants which
were at the laundry on Route Vallon. TOMMY gave him
the thirty cents and a few minutes later KOUZMINSKY
brought the clothes. Still later at the "Rouss"
Restaurant TOMMY took from his pocket a ring and two
medals and gave them to me. Having placed the ring on
my finger, I gave one medal to KOUZMINSKY and the other
I threw on the street in Route Pere Robert.
    From the "Rouss" Restaurant we made our way to the
"Poland" Restaurant, 771/15 Avenue Joffre, where TOMMY
dressed himself in the shirt and pants that KOUZMINSKY
had brought. He kept his footwear, however. We packed
his cap and waterproof in a newspaper, and left the
package with the owner of the "Poland" Restaurant.
    About 10 a.m. myself, TOMMY, KOUZMINSKY and a
Netherlander known as "PONTY" went to 682/6 Rue Bourgeat,
home of one Georges LITVINSKY, in whose place were a
pair of my shoes, which I took. Then with TOMMY I made
my way back to the "Poland" Restaurant by ricsha. There
TOMMY took off his own footwear, donned my shoes and said
it would be necessary to sell his uniform and boots to
anyone. I took the waterproof and boots, and leaving
Lane 771, offered them for sale to Chinese pedestrians.
Nobody wanted to purchase them. Then I handed them
to KOUZMINSKY and told him to go and sell them on Peking
Road. At 1 p.m. (?) (original says 1 a.m.), I crossed
over to Hongkew with a German friend whom I encountered
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

此后，我们三人前往贝当路上的“鲁斯”餐馆。
    在这家餐馆，我们要了一瓶啤酒和半瓶伏特加。过了一会儿，在餐馆里，汤米要求为他找一套便服。库兹明斯基告诉他，如果给他30美分，他可以从瓦隆路的洗衣店带来一件衬衫和一条裤子。汤米给了他30美分，几分钟后库兹明斯基带来了衣服。更晚些时候，在“鲁斯”餐馆，汤米从口袋里拿出一枚戒指和两枚勋章交给我。我将戒指戴在手指上，把一枚勋章给了库兹明斯基，另一枚我扔在了贝当路的街上。
    离开“鲁斯”餐馆后，我们前往霞飞路771/15号的“波兰”餐馆，汤米在那里换上了库兹明斯基带来的衬衫和裤子。但他保留了自己的鞋履。我们将他的军帽和雨衣用报纸包好，寄存在“波兰”餐馆老板处。
    上午10时左右，我、汤米、库兹明斯基以及一名被称为“庞蒂”（PONTY）的荷兰人前往勃艮第路682/6号，即乔治·利特温斯基（Georges LITVINSKY）的住所，那里有一双我的鞋子，我将其取走。然后我与汤米乘人力车返回“波兰”餐馆。在那里，汤米脱下自己的鞋履，穿上我的鞋子，并说需要将他的制服和靴子卖给任何人。我拿走雨衣和靴子，离开771弄，向中国行人兜售。无人购买。随后我将它们交给库兹明斯基，让他去北京路出售。下午1时（？）（原文写的是凌晨1时），我与一位在德国朋友一起穿过虹口，这位朋友是我在

page_data.en:
- 3 -

in a billiard hall at 613/24 Avenue Joffre. When
I returned from Hongkew at 3 p.m. (original says 3 a.m.),
I found KOUZMINSKY in the restaurant at 771/1 Avenue
Joffre where he gave me fifty cents, the results of the
sale of TOMMY's shoes.

Signed :- NOSKOFF.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

霞飞路613/24号的一家台球厅遇到的。当我于下午3时（原文写的是凌晨3时）从虹口回来时，我在霞飞路771/1号的餐馆里找到了库兹明斯基，他给了我50美分，这是出售汤米鞋子所得。

签名：- 诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）。

page_data.en:
September 30, 1938.

Activities of a British deserter and two Russian loafers.

I have to report that at 2.30 p.m. to-day, a
female Russian, Anna G. DEMINA, aged 31, residing at
Apartment 2, 118/9 Route des Soeurs, dancing partner
at the Little Club, Bubbling Well Road, came to the
office and made the following statement :-

Yesterday in the "Dejourny" Russian Restaurant, she
met a British soldier in uniform. She invited him to
come to her room and spend the night of September 29/30
with her.

At 7 a.m. this morning, immediately after the
departure of the soldier, DEMINA noticed that a nickel
wrist-watch, valued at $6, of Japanese make, had dis-
appeared from her dressing table. The watch belongs to
an American marine.

At noon she returned to the "Dejourny" Restaurant
where she met her nocturnal lover in civilian clothes.
She then commenced to reproach him with having stolen
the watch.

The Briton admitted having taken the watch and
then having pawned it and promised DEMINA that he would
go and redeem it. He left but did not return which
caused the woman to make a report to the Police.

Being in possession of information that a British
deserter was probably involved, I advised Bubbling Well
Police Station (D.S. WEEKS), who confirmed our beliefs
and warned the British Military Police, who succeeded
in finding the culprit in the Mallet district and
bringing him to our offices.

On the orders of Mr. CRESTON and on the indications
of the soldier, detective LOUKNITSKY proceeded to the
page_data.zh:
1938年9月30日。

一名英国逃兵和两名俄罗斯流浪汉的活动。

我必须报告，今天下午2时30分，一名俄罗斯女子安娜·G·杰米娜（Anna G. DEMINA），31岁，居住于姐妹路（Route des Soeurs）118/9号2室，静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）“小俱乐部”舞女，来到办公室并作了如下陈述：-

昨天在“德茹尔尼”俄罗斯餐馆，她遇到了一名身穿制服的英国士兵。她邀请他来她的房间，与他共度9月29/30日夜。

今天上午7时，士兵刚离开，杰米娜就注意到她梳妆台上的一块镀镍腕表不见了，该表价值6美元，日本制造。这块手表属于一名美国海军陆战队员。

中午她回到“德茹尔尼”餐馆，在那里遇到了她昨夜的情人，此时他已换上便服。她随即开始指责他偷了手表。

这名英国人承认拿了手表并将其典当，并向杰米娜承诺他会去赎回。他离开了但没有回来，导致该女子向警方报案。

鉴于掌握的信息表明可能涉及一名英国逃兵，我通知了静安寺路巡捕房（D.S. WEEKS），他们证实了我们的推测并警告了英国宪兵队，后者成功在马勒区（Mallet district）找到了罪犯并将其带到我们的办公室。

根据克雷斯顿先生（Mr. CRESTON）的命令以及该士兵的指认，侦探卢克尼茨基（LOUKNITSKY）前往

page_data.en:
- 2 -

"Dejourny" Restaurant, 771/1 Avenue Joffre, where the
following two Russians were arrested and brought to our
offices: -

1. Vladimir NOSKOFF (alias MONGOL), 26, residing at
164 Route Vallon.

2. Eugene KOUZMINSKY, 24, Room 10, 697/2 Avenue Joffre.

A visit paid to the Hung Teh Pawnshop, 7 Route Pere
Robert, revealed that the watch in question was pawned
by the British soldier for $4, but that it was redeemed
some hours later by an unknown Chinese.

The British soldier, Private Thomas CLARK was taken
away by Sergeant Richard HIGGINS of the British Military
Police.

Interrogation of the two Russians who were the
companions of the deserter in his activities in the
Concession this morning, allowed the following facts to
be established: -

The soldier was met by the Russians in the "Dejourny"
Restaurant at 7 a.m. and as he was without funds the
trio proceeded to the above mentioned pawnshop to pawn
the watch which the Englishman had stolen from DEMINA.

The pawning took place with the assistance of
NOSKOFF who marked in Russian the pawn ticket received
by the soldier.

From the pawnshop they proceeded to the "Rouss" Res-
taurant, Route Pere Robert where they drunk beer and
vodka and the Englishman, slightly inebriated, presented
his two medals and a copper ring to the Russians. The
intoxicated soldier then commenced to declare that he
no longer desired to remain in the army but that he
wished to remain always with the Russians.

He asked them if civilian clothing could be procured
for him, upon which KOUZMINSKY, who had given the laundry-
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

霞飞路771/1号的“德茹尔尼”餐馆，在那里逮捕了以下两名俄罗斯人并带到我们的办公室：-

1. 弗拉基米尔·诺斯科夫（Vladimir NOSKOFF）（别名 MONGOL），26岁，居住于瓦隆路164号。

2. 叶夫根尼·库兹明斯基（Eugene KOUZMINSKY），24岁，霞飞路697/2号10室。

对贝当路7号洪德当铺（Hung Teh Pawnshop）的走访显示，涉案手表由该英国士兵以4美元典当，但几小时后被一名身份不明的中国人赎回。

英国士兵托马斯·克拉克（Thomas CLARK）二等兵由英国宪兵队理查德·希金斯（Richard HIGGINS）中士带走。

对这两名俄罗斯人的审讯揭示了今早他们在租界内伴随逃兵活动的事实如下：-

这名士兵于上午7时在“德茹尔尼”餐馆被俄罗斯人遇到，由于他没有资金，三人前往上述当铺典当了英国人从杰米娜那里偷来的手表。

典当是在诺斯科夫的协助下进行的，他在士兵收到的当票上用俄语做了标记。

离开当铺后，他们前往贝当路的“鲁斯”餐馆，在那里喝了啤酒和伏特加，这名英国人微醺之下将他的两枚勋章和一个铜戒指送给了俄罗斯人。这名醉酒的士兵随后开始宣称他不再想留在军队里，而是希望永远与俄罗斯人在一起。

他问他们是否能搞到便服，对此，库兹明斯基曾将洗衣店——

page_data.en:
- 3 -

man at 182 Route Vallon a shirt and a pair of pants to
be washed, replied in the affirmative asking for 30 cents
to pay the laundry bill. The sum was handed to him and
some minutes later KOUZMINSKY brought the Englishman
the garments.

Then the trio went to the "Poland" Restaurant, 771/15
Avenue Joffre, where CLARK changed his uniform for civilian
dress, keeping, however, his service boots with him. His
cap and waterproof were wrapped up in a newspaper and
hidden in a corner of the restaurant.

Remembering that one Georges LITVINSKY, residing at
682/6B, Rue Bourgeat had a pair of his shoes on the
premises, NOSKOFF with the British soldier, KOUZMINSKY
and a Netherlander whose name is said to be PILEN, pro-
ceeded to the address and there secured the pair of
black shoes.

On return to the "Dejourny" Restaurant, the soldier
took off his service footwear and put on the shoes that
NOSKOFF had just secured. He then proposed that the
Russian sell his military issue boots, the waterproof
and service cap.

NOSKOFF took the first two objects with him and
vainly visited several Chinese second hand shops in the
neighbourhood, which refused to purchase the stuff
apparently because it was of obvious military origin.

Not being successful, he returned to Lane 771 Avenue
Joffre and instructed KOUZMINSKY to go and sell the stuff
in Peking Road for $4. The latter proceeded to Peking
Road where he was only able to dispose of the footgear
for 60 cents, the waterproof being of a military pattern
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

在瓦隆路（Route Vallon）182号，一名男子将一件衬衫和一条裤子交给某人清洗，对方予以应允，并索要30美分作为洗衣费。该笔款项已交付给他，几分钟后，库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）将这些衣物送还给了那名英国人。

随后，这三人前往位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）771/15号的“波兰”（Poland）餐馆，克拉克（CLARK）在此将军服换成了便服，但仍随身携带其军用靴。他的军帽和雨衣被包裹在报纸中，藏匿于餐馆的一角。

诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）想起居住在布尔热亚路（Rue Bourgeat）682/6B号的乔治·利特文斯基（Georges LITVINSKY）处有一双他的鞋子，于是偕同那名英国士兵、库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）以及一名据称名为皮伦（PILEN）的荷兰人，前往该地址并取回了那双黑鞋。

回到“德茹尔尼”（Dejourny）餐馆后，这名士兵脱下了军用鞋履，换上了诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）刚取回的鞋子。随后，他提议由这名俄国人出售其配发的军用靴、雨衣和军帽。

诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）带走了前两样物品，走访了附近几家中国旧货店，但均遭拒绝收购，原因显然是这些物品具有明显的军用来源特征。

由于未能成功出手，他返回霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）771号弄堂，指示库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）前往北京路以4美元的价格出售这些物品。后者前往北京路，但仅以60美分的价格处理掉了鞋履，而因雨衣属军用制式，未能找到买家。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

not finding a buyer.

At 3 p.m. KOUZMINSKY returned to Lane 771 Avenue
Joffre and gave 50 cents to NOSKOFF, keeping 10 cents
for himself.

Just at this moment the two Russians were arrested
and the cap, waterproof, and a medal belonging to the
English soldier were found on KOUZMINSKY and a copper
ring of Clark's on NOSKOFF's finger.

On Mr. Creston's instructions, statements from the
Russians, required by the British Military Police, were
taken and NOSKOFF and KOUZMINSKY (the latter in an
advanced stage of intoxication) were placed in the cells.
The two Russians having acted under the influence of
drink in this case there is no criminal intention on
their part, the British soldier having been the first to
give them his clothes to sell.

Anne DEMINA was advised to hold herself at the
disposal of the British Military Authorities in regard
to the stolen watch.

Enquiries are being conducted to ascertain under
what circumstances the pawn ticket for the watch came
the hands of the unknown Chinese who redeemed it.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

下午3时，库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）返回霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）771号弄堂，交给诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）50美分，自留10美分。

就在此时，两名俄国人被捕。在库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）身上搜出了军帽、雨衣以及属于该名英国士兵的一枚勋章，而在诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）的手指上则发现了克拉克（Clark）的一枚铜戒指。

根据克雷斯顿先生（Mr. Creston）的指示，应英国宪兵的要求，对这两名俄国人进行了问话笔录，并将诺斯科夫（NOSKOFF）和库兹明斯基（KOUZMINSKY）（后者处于严重醉酒状态）关入拘留所。鉴于本案中两名俄国人的行为系受酒精影响所致，且是该英国士兵首先主动将其衣物交给他们出售，故认定他们并无犯罪意图。

已告知安妮·杰米娜（Anne DEMINA），就失窃手表一事，听候英国军事当局处置。

目前正在进行调查，以查明那张手表当票是如何落入那名赎回手表的身份不明的中国人手中的。
